# Upstream implementations

TRASA includes complete pinned source snapshots for its upstream methods, together with their original training, preprocessing, inference, evaluation, configuration, and license files.

| Source | Included code | Revision |
|---|---|---|
| [LDTR](https://github.com/knowledge-computing/LDTR) | [ldtr/](ldtr/README.md) | `eaf5c9f3e66ca0181ea98fe4378420107b8af296` |
| [SAM-Road](https://github.com/htcr/sam_road) | [sam_road/](sam_road/README.md) | `04b67c503f120ecff2b2dc5a2041ea6d300e306a` |
| [SAM](https://github.com/htcr/segment-anything-road) | [sam_road/sam/](sam_road/sam/README.md) | `6fdee8f2727f4506cfbbe553e23b895e27956588` |

[sources.json](sources.json) records revisions and the manuscript archive hash. [upstream-files.json](upstream-files.json) contains SHA256 checksums for every included source/reference file; the test suite verifies all 205 files. SAM-Road's two SAM submodule names reference the same included SAM tree. Generated bytecode and build metadata are excluded.

TRASA imports adapted architecture components from `src/trasa/vendor/`; normal execution does not require installing the upstream experiment frameworks. The full snapshots provide the original baseline code and a reference for the adaptations. Native baseline execution requires each upstream README's separate environment and real compatible datasets/checkpoints; see [the reproduction guide](../REPRODUCING.md#external-baselines).

File-level notices and upstream license texts are retained. SAM-Road uses MIT; SAM and Deformable DETR/DETR components retain their Apache-2.0 licenses. The pinned LDTR repository has no top-level license, so no blanket license is assigned to its source or unrelated upstream material.
